payload.rationale: No current data were supplied, so this is a base-rate judgment. Through 2025, US housing starts (SAAR) mostly ran between roughly 1.25M and 1.45M, averaging around 1.33–1.36M, with single-family starts drifting lower under elevated mortgage rates and high new-home inventory while multifamily was volatile and occasionally boosted the headline. A 1.300M threshold therefore sits near, and slightly below, the center of the recent distribution: most 2025 prints exceeded it, but a few (e.g., May 2025 ~1.26M) fell below, and later 2025 readings hovered close to 1.30M. For September 2026 I have no observed 2026 data; plausible transfer assumptions are that modestly lower mortgage rates by 2026 offer some support, offset by weak builder sentiment and affordability constraints, leaving the central expectation near 1.30–1.35M with a monthly standard deviation of roughly 60–80K. That implies a modest lean toward YES. Too high if: the single-family downtrend continued or accelerated into 2026, a recession or labor-market weakness cut demand, or multifamily starts slumped, pushing the level structurally into the 1.2M range. Too low if: rate cuts through 2026 revived single-family construction or multifamily rebounded, putting starts comfortably in the 1.35–1.45M range. Note the resolution depends on the first-published September 2026 figure (as shown on Trading Economics), not later revisions.
limitations: No 2026 housing, rate, or macro data supplied; estimate relies on 2025-and-earlier background knowledge.
Unknown trend in mortgage rates, Fed policy, and builder conditions during 2026.
Monthly starts are noisy and heavily revised; first-print outcome near the threshold is close to a coin flip.
Potential release delays (e.g., government shutdown) could affect timing but not the resolution rule.
